subject.title: [Refactor] Abstract OAuth flow parameters out of LLM transport core

question: Should OpenClaw add a new LLM transport-level OAuth configuration contract despite the existing provider-owned auth and runtime-preparation hooks?
rationale: The report proposes a permanent core API boundary but provides no concrete parameter or consumer proving the existing provider seams are inadequate, so repository architecture alone cannot establish that another contract should exist.

options.title: Require a concrete gap first
options.body: Ask for the exact hardcoded parameters and a blocked provider or caller, then add only the narrow generic seam that the example proves necessary.

options.title: Adopt a transport OAuth contract
options.body: Approve a new injected contract if transport owners want OAuth flow policy standardized below provider plugins despite the additional compatibility surface.

options.title: Retain current provider hooks
options.body: Decline the new contract if all required values can already be prepared through provider auth and runtime-auth hooks.

recommendation.title: Require a concrete gap first
recommendation.body: Ask for the exact hardcoded parameters and a blocked provider or caller, then add only the narrow generic seam that the example proves necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: The available routing evidence most directly connects this person to the provider-auth side of the proposed boundary.
